People who are generally unhappy, dissatisfied with life, or lonely tend to not want children. If you belong in any of these categories, or you are young, address the issues and the desire may return.

But I bet you already knew that, didn't you? The question is how: Well, the same advice that I keep giving around, you need to understand your underlying issues, as to why you think you don't have anything to offer a child, or why it would be a bad thing. Then, you need to take risks and actually meet someone; the desire to have children with that person might arise, and if you're both interested in a long-term relationship, I don't see why not.

I don't want children; I am about to turn 26, and I never have. A few years back, the reason was that I did not want to pass on my undesirable traits (short, skinny), but as I grew older, I realized that these traits are actually more of a blessing than a curse, so that concern faded. The next reason was that I didn't think I could take care of a child as I wasn't responsible enough; again, that concern has passed. Now my reason is that I am experiencing a high point in my life and I don't want to stop right now because it feels good, plus I don't have the financial stability for a child.
